input.prompt: Continue the supplied camera frame as one documentary interview take. SUBJECT: the reference bakery owner, greying dark hair tied back; cream long-sleeve shirt, flour-dusted charcoal apron, brown straps, lavalier unchanged. Preserve the visible face, age, hairline, nose, asymmetry and skin texture of the reference; do not beautify or add new facial marks. Fine lines and uneven skin reflect the existing side light. SET: same wood and tile bakery, bread shelves and window on screen right. LIGHT: unchanged warm morning daylight from screen right, stable exposure and white balance. CAMERA: eye-level medium close-up with the original headroom and lens perspective; locked tripod, no zoom, no pan. ENTRY: seated center-left; travel stationary; shoulders relaxed, head upright, mouth closed, gaze slightly camera-right; props microphone clipped to the same apron strap; hands empty below frame. PERFORMANCE: eyes attend to the same interviewer just camera-right, with tiny refocusing movements and unforced irregular blinking. Quiet breath moves the shoulders; one slight head inclination accompanies the thought, then settles. Hands rest low in her lap, not rigid; no finger-counting or presenting objects. Sleeve folds respond only to body movement; stray hairs remain settled in still air. Understated conversational delivery, not a broad smile or theatrical eyebrow lift. AUDIO: say exactly once in natural British English: "It builds the schedule around that, and everyone sees it update." Begin promptly, complete the thought without restarting, then let the lips close naturally for a brief listening pause. Quiet bakery room tone, no music. EXIT: shoulders relaxed, head upright, mouth closed, gaze slightly camera-right; seated center-left; travel stationary; props microphone clipped to the same apron strap; hands empty below frame. Same light, set and camera throughout. No cuts, subtitles, titles, logos or graphic overlays.
